answer: A triboelectric fabric woven into clothing generates charge from every rub of cloth against cloth, and the harvested energy is logged per day. An identity can rest on that log: the hollow weave of the fabric holds the charge, a relic loom pattern gives each garment a known output curve, and the ferrous threads woven in as electrodes carry the current to the meter. Only the garment that moved through those days can present the matching harvest log.
